title: For those building games with AI: where do you personally draw the line, and how do players react when you disclose it?
author: BadMuthaJoJo
selftext:
I'm trying to figure out where I land on AI in games, and I think people actually building with it have the most useful view.



Some uses seem uncontroversial to me, like dev tools and brainstorming. Others seem to cause a reaction as soon as players find out, like AI voices or art in the finished game. The line looks different depending on whether the player ever sees or hears the result.



Where do you draw it in your own projects? Do you disclose, and if so, how have players responded? Has anyone changed their approach after feedback?

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: this is the most posted thing on this sub, try looking at past results, you'll likely get more answers. Its anywhere from lying to full disclousre. personally just do what the store fronts want and no more

replies.author: Stinky_You
replies.body: Looks like bot history or something. Same or similar post in like +5 different subs

comments.author: theweeJoe
comments.body: Always disclose straight up. Ignore the haters, let players find your game is good on its own merits. My game wouldn't exist without AI so I make no apologies

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: I'm only making one game so far, but the webpage you go to says "Vibe Coded Games" so anyone not into it can exit before they even try it. Most people tell me the game is great or give me feedback. The people who call it "slop" have said things showing the OBVIOUSLY never played the game at all. I don't deal with it, I don't interact. My games are AI, they wouldn't exist otherwise. Shut up, I'm working.

comments.author: revel911
comments.body:
The question is:

Are you building this game for:

Yourself, for fun, to make money? And does AI even matter in how you built it? There are people showing slop that entirely interested by AI and then there are people showing amazing ideas they created and using AI as a tool to make their idea a tangible item. That’s a huge difference.

replies.author: Brettinabox
replies.body: This. People are what make the difference in anything. AI has always been a tool but the person lets the tool do so much that they arent investing their creativity into it. Gotta have standards.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
the first thing i talk about with people is how i use ai. when i then tell them to playtest noone is "wondering" if its ai.

the people buying my first game didnt care much either but there werent many tbh

comments.author: Mobius2025
comments.body: If I use AI to create a game, that game, at the very least, is free to play. For some games, I will also provide an open source archive of all the files. I guess where I draw the line is consciously trying to replace games created by actual people.

comments.author: TheVoyant
comments.body:
Wherever I feel like, it's a small amount of people who are closed minded.   
They eventually will lose, if they're not ok with Ai games today, they will be in a decade.

Just get to work cut out the noise, do your thing.   
If it's good, it's good.

comments.author: OffWhiteStudios
comments.body:
I don’t hide it at all (couldn’t even if I wanted to). It hasn’t stopped the game from doing well and I have had 0 issues with “anti’s”

There are many many people who don’t care if a game uses AI, they just want it to be good.

If you will believe it, I have even done fan art contests (both AI and non-AI categories) and had actually people with artistic drawing talent submitting fan art of AI generated characters from the game.

If you find your audience (usually by not hiding your AI use) the community you build can actually be really great and drama free. 

That said, I also stay away from some popular spaces I know my game won’t be welcome for this reason. It is a bit sad a vocal 20-50% can control what the remaining 80-50% gets to see. 

As an AI game dev just try not to hide things or trick people. Advertise the game uses AI and let it stand out by its quality and the unique touch you put into it!

comments.author: Sorrytokeepyouwaitin
comments.body: I genuinely don’t see the point in disclosing since I make all the assets myself. Crazy that people would still have a shit storm about it even though I can code it all by hand anyway. They just want me to waste 100s of hours of my own time fixing typos and writing the same shit over and over so they can feel secure in their own beliefs. Wanting me to waste my own time on this planet to appease their ideology is whack.

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body:
Always disclose, it filters the worst people from your game.

As for tool use. Voice. Its just not there yet, and it's to personal.

comments.author: Brettinabox
comments.body: So far its been a personal project, not really to make any return but to learn how to make games and how to build the systems that i like playing. I like how vast procedural generation works in rimworld so im using that in my project. At some later point that it doesnt get traction because of coding with AI, then i might be more comfortable making one without it.

comments.author: Small_Friendship_659
comments.body: 100% disclose.  People deserve the right to make their own choices.  I'm excited by AI and I want to share what it's enabled me to do.  Why be weird about it?  Respect people, respect their choices, and be proud of the tools and what it's enabled you to do.  If you're doing something shady - like ripping off someone elses ideas whole cloth, or shoveling out ai garbage with no intent or passion - then your heart is in the wrong place to begin with.

comments.author: Own_Badger6076
comments.body:
Honestly no, fuck em, there's no reason to disclose it. 

If you were going to disclose it though, the line i would use is any use of AI Art related assets, but if you're just using it for code generation then no.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body:
My line is that if it looks good or not.

Its simple really, the question is would I be out off by this? And if the answer is yes, that means the current state is not good enough.
